newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB says Australia winter wheat rises A$10/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB says Australia winter wheat rises A$10/t.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Tuesday the price for winter wheat had increased by A$10.00 to A$130.00 a tonne.
The AWB linked the rise in the estimated equity of the AWB Winter Wheat (AWW) pool to domestic and international price gains in grains and underlying support from hedging programmes.

In a statement, AWB Victorian state manager Chris Ayers said the AWW arangements required growers to re-deliver all their crop to the AWB. "The premium for our Australian Winter Wheat (AWW) over other feed pools represents the benefits of the tight re-delivery requirements," Ayers said.

"Having a firm indication of the amount of winter wheat we have to market this year allowed us to implement more aggressive price risk management strategies much earlier in the season to capitalise on higher prices prevailing at that time," he said.
The pick-up in the winter wheat price was also supported by the general lift in world grain prices, as reflected by increases in the AWB's Feed wheat pool.

"The recent A$20.00 a tonne increase in estimated equity for the AWB Feed wheat pool was a welcome turnaround for growers of all feed grains as this will provide support to all prices this season," he said.

A further key factor has been the renewed strength in international markets over recent weeks along with smaller-than-expected receivals of downgraded wheat in Western Austtralia, New South Wales and Queensland states, Ayers said.
The AWW pool is available to all AWB winter wheat producers (Lawson and Paterson varieties).
Other red wheat producers have access to the new Australian Standard Red (ASR) wheat pool, the equity for which has been posted at A$130 a tonne delivered Melbourne end user, the AWB said.
